what_its_for: This antibiotic combination is used to treat bacterial infections, including ear infections, sinus infections, pneumonia, skin infections, and urinary tract infections. Amoxicillin kills the bacteria, while clavulanate helps amoxicillin work better by blocking bacteria that would otherwise make the antibiotic stop working.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with a full glass of water. It is best to take it at the START of a meal or snack to reduce stomach upset and help your body absorb it better. Swallow extended-release tablets (XR) whole — do not crush, chew, or split them. You may crush or chew regular tablets or chewable tablets. If using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before each use and measure your dose carefully with the measuring spoon or syringe that came with your medicine — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. Take ALL of your doses even if you start feeling better early. Stopping too soon can let bacteria grow back and make your infection harder to treat.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose based on your infection, your age, and your kidney function. A common adult dose is one tablet (875 mg/125 mg) taken twice a day, or one tablet (500 mg/125 mg) taken three times a day. Children's doses are based on body weight and are usually given twice a day. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's exact instructions. Do not take more than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one, as this could cause unwanted side effects.
storage: Store tablets and chewable tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C–25°C). Keep them away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture — do NOT store in the bathroom. Keep the liquid (suspension) in the refrigerator after mixing, but do NOT freeze it. Throw away any unused liquid after 10 days. Keep all medicines out of the reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids that contain magnesium or aluminum right before or after your dose, as they can reduce how well this medicine works. Avoid alcohol while taking this antibiotic, as it may increase side effects like upset stomach and dizziness. Do not take extra doses or share this medicine with others. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL other medicines you take, especially blood thinners like warfarin (Coumadin), methotrexate, or probenecid, as they can interact with this antibiotic.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: a severe allergic reaction (rash, hives, itching, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, trouble breathing, or dizziness); severe watery or bloody diarrhea, which could be a sign of a serious gut infection called C. difficile (this can happen even weeks after finishing the antibiotic); yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice) or dark urine; severe skin reactions such as peeling, blistering, or mouth sores; or seizures. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve after 2 to 3 days of treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within 2 to 3 days of starting this medicine. However, it is very important to finish the ENTIRE course of antibiotics your doctor prescribed, even if you feel completely better before you finish. This helps make sure all the bacteria are killed and prevents the infection from coming back or becoming resistant to antibiotics.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It is generally considered safe during pregnancy, but your doctor needs to weigh the benefits and risks for you. BREASTFEEDING: Small amounts of this medicine pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor if you are breastfeeding, as it is usually considered safe but may cause fussiness or diarrhea in the baby. CHILDREN: Doses are carefully calculated by weight for children. Use only the liquid suspension or chewable tablets that are prescribed for your child — do not use adult tablets. KIDNEY PROBLEMS: If you have kidney disease, your doctor may lower your dose or change how often you take this medicine. Make sure your doctor knows about any kidney problems. PENICILLIN OR CEPHALOSPORIN ALLERGY: Tell your doctor and pharmacist immediately if you are allergic to penicillin, amoxicillin, or any cephalosporin antibiotic before taking this medicine, as you may also be allergic to this medication.
